forefront: Entirely true, and this profile leads with it.
healthy: The Faith claims ~5–8 million members worldwide.
history: Baháʼu'lláh founded the Faith in 19th-century Iran and Ottoman exile, out of the Bábí movement.
branches: The Faith is overwhelmingly a single unified body, and the Covenant structure has been unusually effective at preventing schism.
reach: Covenant-breaker designation obliges members to shun the designated person entirely, including family — the sharpest sanction in the system.
techniques: Thirty named techniques from domestic-abuse and social-psychology research, applied to institutions, in the eight stages of the cycle.
loops: The seven loops below show how the practices connect, so that each step makes the next one easier and the last step feeds the first.
say-do: In the scholarly disenrollment episodes, the individual departs and the review policy remains.
cost: Scholars publishing critical history have faced review pressure and disenrollment episodes.
ledger: The administrative order benefits through its continuity and narrative control, and unity is an institutional asset.
who-gets-hurt: They fall hardest where a person has the least power inside the institution, or none, and the fewest places to go outside it.
tiers: Most of the institution's work is done below the House of Justice, by people who see decisions without making them.
voices: They were imprisoned for a second decade for administering their community.
questions: If a designated covenant-breaker's family must shun them, ask which teaching about unity requires a mother to stop speaking to her son.
leaving: Resigning is not the same as being declared a "covenant-breaker".
